question: Judged against the code it exercises, is this test tautological (its expected value is computed the same way the code computes it, so it cannot disagree with the code), implementation-coupled (it reaches past its seam into private functions, source text or internal collaborators, so a behaviour-preserving refactor breaks it), or ok (it drives a public surface or a deep module's stable interface and compares against an independent expected value)?

label_help.tautological: expected value restates the code's own computation (same operation, same helper, or the code's own output); passes by construction. Takes precedence when a test is also coupled.
label_help.implementation-coupled: reaches internals: imports or rewrites private helpers, mocks internal collaborators, reads or edits source text, asserts call counts; breaks on a rename that keeps behaviour.
label_help.ok: drives a public surface (CLI, HTTP, UI) or the stable interface of a deep module, public or internal, never a private helper or shallow wrapper (fakes only at external boundaries such as PATH stubs, fake services, OS namespaces) and compares to an independent literal or oracle.

state_shape: 'Test:' the test excerpt, trimmed from its source, then optionally 'Code it exercises:' with the minimum of the code under test or a one-line note naming the public surface. No reviewer verdict, finding class or label.
